newsitem.title: USA: C-Tec to split into three public companies.
newsitem.headline: C-Tec to split into three public companies.

text.p: C-Tec Corp., a Princeton, N.J.-based telecommunications company, said Thursday it plans to separate its operations into three separate, publicly traded companies.
It is anticipated that the spin-offs to shareholders will occur by year-end.
The three publicly held companies will each have separate boards of directors and trade on The Nasdaq Stock Market.
C-Tec said it does not expect staff reductions or employee layoffs as a result of the separation of the businesses.

Under the plan, one segment will be RCN Corp., consisting of RCN Telecom Services, which provides video and telecommunications services in Boston and New York, the New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania cable television operations, and the investment in Megacable S.A. de C.V., Mexico's largest cable operator.
A second separate company will be CTCo, which will consist of local telephone operations and related engineering business.
The third company will be C-TEC Cable Systems of Michigan Inc., which will consist of the company's cable television operations in Michigan, including its 62 percent interest in Mercom Inc.

"As we announced last year, C-TEC is committed to bridging the gap between the true value of our businesses and the value currently perceived by the investment community," said David C. McCourt, chairman and chief executive of C-TEC.
"After careful evaluation, we have decided the best alternative to realise the value of our businesses is through separation into three separately traded companies," he said.
C-Tec stock was up $1.375 at $28 in morning trading on Nasdaq.
